items.name: Note for the boss
items.contents: One of the captives made a run for the bridge. Shame Baines put a bullet in the back of her head before she made it. Wanted to draw out the other cultist freaks and have a good, clean hunt: my patrol has been lookin' lean and hungry lately. The excitement might give 'em a kick up the ass, too. Some are getting lazy. Nothing to worry about though, boss. I'll beat 'em into shape.

items.name: Note from Bill
items.contents:
Daniel,
So very sorry to hear about the recent intrusion. Must've been just awful, feeling totally helpless to have prevented those rioters from marauding around, knowing you'd failed to protect what's yours.
Please accept the enclosed - a little something so you can have at least some protection in the future.
And if things get particularly bleak, you can always turn it around.
Bill Garrahan

items.name: Note from Jen
items.contents:
There is price for being an asshole. For you, that price is going to be gold. When we finally get to that gold bullion, if we get there, I'm going to take some for myself. Ten bars is probably what I'll be able to handle. You'll never see me do it. I'm just going to pop on my stealth field, take that gold and walk out of there. And you'll never be the wiser until you read this. Don't bother to try and find me. I'm leaving Appalachia with my loot. Just remember, there is a price for being an asshole.
Jen

items.name: Note from Miller
items.contents:
I'm getting closer. I can feel it.
Growing up in West Virginia, I've heard the stories since I was a kid. And I always knew the truth - that the Mothman is real! He's real, and I'm going to find him, no matter what it takes.
To all my friends - sorry for leaving you behind, and I know you'd come with me if you could. Some journeys you've just got to make alone. But you're with me in spirit - just like I'll always be with you. West Virginia forever!
Evan "Limbless" Miller
P.S. Zack, I hope you still have that shotgun ammo. I may not have found the Mothman yet, but I did run into the Grafton Monster, and that thing is a BEAST!

items.name: Note to Pete
items.contents:
Dearest Pete,
Aren't I blessed to be taken in by such lovely people as yourself? I was wondering if you'd like to show me around the Tunnel of Love when it's set up? Come on! Say yes! It'll be fun!
Sunshine and smiles,
Betty

items.name: Old Guns
items.contents: Thought about looting this place, but why? Nothing but antiques here. Try loading a black powder pistol when a Raider is swinging a machete at your face.

items.name: Operation Watoga
items.contents:
Operation Watoga
Mission Status: Aborted
The cost is just too high.
Once we have the Scorchbeasts under control, we can again consider additional forays into Watoga.

items.name: Orders from Maria Chavez
items.contents:
Paul,
I need you to make the monthly scouting run to Vault 76. Those doors have to open some time.
Don't take risks. Observe for a few days and come back.
-Maria

items.name: Orders from Melody
items.contents:
1. Meet up at checkpoint near Big Bend Tunnel West. 2. Assault team charges in and pushes back the Scorched.
3. Demo team sets charges. 4. Get out of there and blow the tunnel. 5. If things go pear-shaped, evacuate the tunnels.

items.name: Pamela's Note
items.contents:
Tom,
I'm leaving this note in case I'm not here when you arrive. Things have been horrible at the church. We're overloaded with people sheltering, praying and suffering. After only a few weeks, our supplies are running low. I've decided to head out with some people to look for food and medicine. If I end up not coming back, don't come looking for me. Stay with the kids, keep them safe and pray with the others.
God help us all.
Pamela

items.name: Password Sheet
items.contents:
How often are those idiots gonna mess things up? This is the third time this week I'm changing the password!
I've sent some of them up to the Shenandoah Visitor Center to "get blessings from the Mothman", but really I wanted them out of my way so they don't ruin Cassidy's big send-off. [pagebreak] Not only do I have to start writing these new passwords down now, so I don't forget, but I am also running out of ideas.
New password is: To peak past Pepper you must pester Pepper's peers to apprise Pepper's Password to pass past Pepper's pier.

items.name: Pat's Journal
items.contents:
[2083/02/07] Dear Diary... Is that how you start a diary? I don't know how you do this sorta thing...
Gunther said it would be good for me... to get some feelings down... to "process the
grief" he said...
I don't even know how to process?... how do you process something that you can't hold?
Anyway... he's the adult. I trust him to know what he's talking about... although am I the adult now too?
I thought we were so lucky that Mom, Pops, Pete and me all survived the bombs. But now it's just Pete and me. I'm responsible for him now... and for the Carnival? Gunther is wrong, this isn't helping at all! I just feel angrier now! Bye!!!
[pagebreak] [2091/09/17] It's been a minute since mom and pops passed. I still miss them every day. But at least I got Pete!
He's a full grown adult now... setting up all the attractions and repairing all sorts. He worries me though - he's never quite gotten over the fact mom and pops are gone.
He is such a sweet soul... I don't think this new world is for him, but he'll battle through! I'm sure! Just gotta make sure I'm there for him...
We've been traveling around much keeping the Carnival going. Making some caps here and there. We've lost so many along the way. It's not always easy to keep strong. Sometimes I don't see the reason to keep going with it all but then I remember Mom and Pops and I continue for them.
[pagebreak] [2094/07/18] I swear I'm going to kill that idiot Del. I found Pete in a ditch today, absolutely pumped on Daddy-O again. He's gonna die one day if Del keeps giving him these Chems. He is wrong. They absolutely do not help him...
I question myself as to why we keep letting him be part of the Carnival... I'll have a chat with Gunther later to get his opinion on it.
I know Pete is not a child anymore but he sure doesn't act like a grown up. I don't know how I'll ever be able to trust him to look after himself. I need to keep him safe. He is the last of my family...
[pagebreak]
[2104/10/05] We've been attacked again and lost a few of our group... they all scattered into different directions trying to get away. I'm not sure they all made it but I sure hope they will all make their way back to us.
We're just gonna keep setting up around the Ash Heap. Hoping they'll see our attractions and come join us again. It's not that easy getting it all set up with the missing workforce, but we've managed before and we'll manage again! And who knows... maybe we'll have a few new travelers join us.

items.name: Percy's Last Note
items.contents:
We've finally managed to take down The Committee.
The lives lost, the crushing battles - it was all worth it.
I hope.
We'll never see the surface, but we know that the people who live there are safe.
I hope someone reads this, someone who can tell our story.
- Percy.

items.name: Phyllis's Note
items.contents:
Mother,
I hope you received my first letter. Things are getting worse here at the resort. These people around us, they don't seem to care about anyone else. I'm hearing them talk about hunting parties and heading to Charleston to take what they want. People are arguing, fighting -
I even saw someone get shot! I'm scared, mother and I want to go home. They say war brings out the worst in mankind. From what I've seen, nothing could be further from the truth.
Stay Safe, Phyllis Mendolsohn

items.name: Prisoner's Note
items.contents:
We ran into some cultists today while doing a pick-up job. Rest of those damn cowards fled. Left me, Patrick, Dustin and Hunter to these freaks.
They took us to some old mineshaft. Freezing down here now that all the adrenaline's settled. [pagebreak] Hell, I've done some sadistic crap with the crew over the years, but having it happen to our guys... makes me feel sick to my stomach. They took Patrick away. Didn't see him again but sure did hear him. Hell of an echo down here. [pagebreak] Seems they need to keep a few of us alive for some ritual, so they won't kill all of us, but that don't stop them from using us for fun. Cut us. Burn us. Bash our heads. Crush our fingers. Flay us alive. Taking stuff right out of our playbook, cept they spend the whole time praising some bug while doing it.
[pagebreak] Least there's some comfort in knowing one of em is a bit different from the others. This Ghoul gal. She's a straight shooter, none of this Mothman nonsense when talking to us. Like she doesn't belong here with these cultists. [pagebreak] Weird thing is, she acts totally different around the others, even though she seems like the boss. Like she's putting on an act. But at least she sneaks us some scraps when they're not around. [pagebreak] If we ever get outta here, I'm done with the Blood Eagles. I can't be part of anything horrific no more. Can't do things like this to people. I need to get out. I'm scared, but I need to get out.
Someone's coming. Maybe this is my chance. I've got to try.

items.name: Raider's Journal Entry 1
items.contents: June 1st Hit a fine jackpot finding this abandoned cabin all the way out here. Looks like it's still held together enough for us to set up. Asher found a robot while digging through all the junk in the bunker. Going to take a look tomorrow and maybe get it runnin again.

items.name: Raider's Journal Entry 2
items.contents: June 7th Don't know how, but I got the robot to boot up. Glad it's workin, but it won't shut up about making moonshine. There are worse things I guess. If it wants to make some of that sweet hooch, we'll take it. I think it'll fit right in with the gang here.

items.name: Raider's Journal Entry 3
items.contents: June 10th Damn, three days later and the robot still ain't shuttin up! The boys are callin it Ned after some drunk blabbermouth we ran into a while back. Felt like it needed a name if it's stickin around. Crazy robot's only interested in moonshine, so it fits. Keeps talking about the stills outside and now somethin about a jamboree. Ned likes to party!

items.name: Raider's Journal Entry 4
items.contents: June 16th This moonshine is damn good! Not too sure how a robot be makin booze, but I ain't complaining. I'll be feeling this tomorrow for damn sure. We're having a big ol' party to celebrate the completion of the new digs, courtesy of Ned o' course. The boys heard some weird noises from outside, but it's probably just Clay, give him a few drinks and he'll wander off good.

items.name: Raider's Journal Entry 5
items.contents: June 17th Ned's hooch ain't for the faint of heart! Gave me and my crew the runs, somethin fierce! Tasted damn good though. Seems those noises from last night been going all morning too, and the boys say they've seen some big ass lizards at the edge of camp. Ned's obsessin over them. Says their venom makes the moonshine special! It has a way of hookin you, but it does wonders for my spirit. Shame it ain't the same for my gut though.

items.name: Raider's Journal Entry 6
items.contents: June 24th Most of the crew has run, they scared of the creatures and saying they been feeling weak. Goddamned cowards! I ain't been feeling too well either, but this is our camp, and I ain't going without a fight. Ah who needs em, huh? Less people here means more of that sweet hooch for me!

items.name: Raider's Journal Entry 7
items.contents: June 29th Oh Ned, my good pal, still stickin with me here when everyone else ran! I'm stuck in bed, and I ain't feelin good at all. Least I've got Ned bringin me more and more moonshine to pass the time. Tasty moonshine, wonderful moonshinneeee! These critters outside are damn loud, they're gettin close to the house. Ah well, let them come see good ol' Slayer.

items.name: Reason to Live
items.contents:
Look at this place. I'm king of the god damned world up here! Who threw the magic beans under my childhood town? Guess a little radiation goes a long way around here. Well, maybe that and some government bullshit. Not sure how you end up in a world like this without the good old government bullshit.
You know, I came here to say my goodbye's and fuck you's to the world, but now maybe I'll stay a little longer. I got a room with a view, and I can't wait to take a piss off this thing.

items.name: Red Rocket Postcard
items.contents: Red Rocket

items.name: Red Water
items.contents:
Not much to do while I wait on a storm. Might be able to catch some rain.
The groundwater--it's poison. Got to everywhere by now. Doesn't matter how thirsty we get--we can't use it.
I can't believe I used to hate rain.

items.name: Reggie's Note
items.contents:
The creature's been chasing me ever since I left the mountains. I don't know why it's followed me this far, but I'm scared that it won't stop until I become its next meal. It's already eaten Dino and the wound in my leg is getting bad. I can barely walk, let alone run away. It will be a miracle if I make it through the night. If I don't, tell Eloise that I love her.
Reggie

items.name: Relocation Note
items.contents:
If anyone comes looking for me, I've taken Winston out to our hunting cabin.
I don't think he's gonna make it, and that's his favorite place so I figured he should spend his last days there.

items.name: Reminder
items.contents:
Note to self...
Talk to Abbie about JD and Brianna. Maybe she can help talk sense into my brother. Brianna is no good. I know she's using him, but he doesn't want to listen to me. Abbie is smart, and JD respects her. She can make him listen.

items.name: Reminder
items.contents:
NOTE TO SELF
Bedroom terminal password written down in HQ office
Just in Case

items.name: Responder's Assignment
items.contents:
There are reports of a survivor group holed up near
who are running low on supplies. I know our rations are limited but bring them these provisions and teach them what you can.

items.name: Responder's Note
items.contents:
Hey idiots, want to get into this safe? No problem! We threw the key off the balcony when you were coming up. Saw it land right on top of the shitter outside!
Pretty sure you walking bricks can't read, so good luck, assholes!

items.name: Responder's Note
items.contents:
A Scorchbeast came on us quick and quiet out of the night sky. We barely escaped with our lives, but now we've all got this sickness.
I didn't think. I just ran. No way in hell they're sticking me in a cage to poke and prod. I'm going to beat this damned Scorched plague. Someone has to be the first to do it, right?

items.name: Rob's Journal
items.contents:
Been walking for days and Miles is getting on everyone's nerves. The guy just doesn't know when to let things go, I swear. There'll be more food to scavenge at the next place, not like it's our fault he dropped his supplies when those dogs chased us back there.
If anything he should be thanking Rebecca for taking the blasted things out...
To be expected I suppose, we're all on edge since we set foot in Shenandoah with that freaky storm looming at the center.
Craig keeps pushing us toward that manor just under the eye of the storm, but I got a bad feeling about this...
It's bad juju is all I'm saying.

items.name: Rodney's Poem
items.contents:
She went out, she got a second opinion Now she's afraid of the light I cut up her credit cards She was coming home
My house we put the mirror of there dogs be Every room he leaves a pyramid There was a worm in it

items.contents:

Stuff I can get on my own: Chicken, tatos, corn, salt and pepper...

items.name: Scavenger's note
items.location: Burn CUT Athens Note Failed Scavenge
items.contents: HOLOTAPE RECORDING *Sounds of a man running and panting* "Oh God oh God oh God" *Sound of metal garbage can being knocked into as man hides* "Shit. I just KNEW Baxter's greed was gonna get us killed" *Woman's scream heard in distance* "Oh God... We saw the signs before we entered, but he made us ignore them! We had a bad feeling when the initial scout group went out and didn't come back. Then Baxter had the BRIGHT IDEA to shout to them...The ferals just came right out of the walls! God we didn't even realize we were surrounded!" *Sound of feral ghouls spotting man and running at him* *Man screams "NOOO!" and recording ends*

items.name: Scavenger's note
items.contents:
If you're reading this, Schmidt got us killed just as we said he would. Athens has been a legend of untouched loot for a reason, but he insisted that we'll not only be fine, but rich beyond worries.
Walking in, Deb shared my sentiment of unease, but Schmidt insisted that the warning signs were too old to be relevant. Setting up camp at the university seemed to prove him right, and by damn did he rub it in. Once set up, he had half of the group head in to scout while the rest of us rested. They've been gone a while now, and it's getting dark. We're starting to worry.
I think I hear things creeping around us, and if we're sprung, I'm not sticking around. And since you're reading this, you shouldn't either.

items.name: Scenarios: Returning from Raleigh's
items.contents:
Scenarios: Returning from Raleigh's
1. Ransacked and nothing found 2. Entry terminal busted 3. Motors and heating coils found! 4. Bunker flooded 5. Motors no longer working 6. Scorched living there 7. Aliens

items.name: Scott's Letter
items.contents:
Dear Peach,
I always knew if the apocalypse came, the biggest threat to survival would be other people. These damn raiders have been harassing me left and right. Now, the Gourmands have started stalking me. There is no way I'm letting anyone cook me up for dinner.
I've holed up in this old trailer next to some radioactive dump site. I figure the rads will keep them away from me, and if I die here, my body will be too toxic for them to eat. Even then, if they're stupid and eat me anyway, I can only hope the radiation in my body would put an end to them.
I sure wish you were here, although you're better off without me. You were right to leave back when I was being a self-righteous prick. I guess this is my way of saying I'm sorry. Hopefully, somehow, you'll know that.
I love you, Peach,
Scott

items.contents:

items.name: Security Guard's Final Goodbye
items.contents:
I feel like a character in one of them pulp horror magazines... I think I'm the only one left. And when I say "left," I don't mean alive, I mean not... turned. Something happened down in the Vault.
[pagebreak] I can hear them outside, banging on the door and shrieking nonsense like "DEMONS" and "SPIRITS". They keep popping and sparking like someone stuck a fork in a power outlet. My terminal's power has been fried, and my lamp keeps flickering, too.
I'm afraid this door won't last much longer. I'm scared. Please God, don't make me one of them...

items.name: Sermon Notes
items.contents:
- We can't drink the water. It turned red. Egypt? - Burns to breathe. Don't panic.
- Don't blame them for working at that plant. Not their fault.
- Judgment has come? - Prayer is all we have now.

items.name: Sgt. Elk's Journal
items.contents:
Been a good chunk of time since the robots took over. Processed more recruits than I ever could, since the bots don't need to sleep, and we can sort of stagger everyone into day/night shifts.
At least the recruits are full of fire, with the war on. Can't say the same for myself. I've gained over ten pounds thanks to how much sitting I do now. Used to be one of Uncle Sam's lean and mean killers, now I'm packing away coffee and donuts like some damn desk jockey.

items.name: Sharon's Angry Letter
items.contents:
Mr. Hayes,
Something must be done about Daniel Whitby. That man is clearly carrying a disease and he needs to be removed from Harpers Ferry before we all become infected!
Have you seen his skin? His hair? He's changing into a monster and unless we exile him, we're all going to end up looking that way. Send him packing right now, or force Ella and Maria to drag him back to the Responders' HQ in Charleston. Whatever it takes.
He's a ticking time bomb, Eddie. Don't wait until it's too late.
Sharon

items.name: Shelley's Letter
items.contents:
Brant,
Remember how crazy you said I was to join up with the Brotherhood of Steel at Camp Venture? How you said I wouldn't be able to hack it, that I'd quit within a week? Well I'm writing to tell you that you were dead wrong. This is where I belong, side-by-side with people who give a crap about this world. Senior Knight Wilson treats me like I'm important, like I matter. Something you never did. I've found my calling, and I'm not coming home. The Brotherhood is my new family now. Now who's laughing?
Shelley

items.contents:
==== TEMP
Romance magazine tips about ways to a man's heart, but it's unclear that this doesn't mean ripping hearts out. Lots said about quality of the heart too.

items.name: Skeleton Extraction Guide
items.contents:
Method for Constructing a Skeleton for General Use -
Step 1: Acquire a Cadaver Step 2: Using a filet knife, remove as much flesh as you can without marking the underlying bones Step 3: Place the cadaver in a wooden box packed with Calcium Oxide. Wait a week. Step 4: Place the remains in a water flow of some kind, like a stream or river. Step 5: Clean off any remaining flesh or ligamentation Step 6: Allow skeleton to dry in the sun. Be wary of predatory birds or wild dogs Step 7: Bleach and mount skeleton
Note: If your tombstone does not read "Rest in Peace", or some variant thereof, you are automatically drafted into the skeleton wars.

items.contents:

Take McCoy's morning watch at the South bridge. It's yours as long as he's in the infirmary or until I can find a replacement.

items.name: Stanley's Note
items.contents:
Senator,
I take great umbrage to the fact that the military has left us stranded at Pleasant Valley. Many of us here are important and relevant members of society, yet we've apparently been left here to rot. I myself contributed a sizable donation to your last campaign and even sent you that rather expensive gift for Christmas last year. It's been several weeks and frankly, I'm beginning to think no one is ever going to show. When I return to D.C., you and I are going to have a long talk about your future, Senator.
Sincerely, Stanley Leek, Esquire

items.name: Stay Away
items.contents:
Gloria,
My rash is spreading. I'm losing some hair too. Writing this so you won't come back to the house. They said it's not contagious but I'm not taking chances. Stay with your sister. I'm afraid to go outside. Afraid that if the soldiers find me, they'll throw me out, or lock me up, or put me in one of those burn pits like they did with the Millers when they died. I'm praying it clears up soon. Maybe you can find me some ointment.
Karl

items.name: Sue Them
items.contents:
You put this recorder in your shirt pocket. It's small, no one will know it's there. I'm serious, Michael.
It's not fair. They "can't help it?" You're just "big boned?"
We'll see what they have to say after we sue them for workplace safety violations!
And don't be your usual idiot self and take this note to work. Throw it away AT HOME!
Also, the fridge forgot to order milk again, pick some up on your way home.
I'll be home late again, don't wait up.

items.name: Surge's Letter
items.contents:
Dear Daddy,
I know you ain't around no more, but I wanted you to know that your little girl made it, thanks to you. I fell in with some decent folks I met up around Appalachia. They're survivors, and they ain't afraid to do what it takes to live to see another day. You'd like them. Well, maybe not all of them. Especially not this guy I've taken a shine to, but you never did think anyone was good enough for me. I still remember you chasing around Hank with a shotgun and that time you accidentally shot Wade in the leg.
I miss you. I know you wanted me to stay, but I couldn't spend another day in that damn bunker. I reckon you understand seeing as how you died down there and I couldn't get your body out anyways.
RIP Daddy, Maxi

A little bit of rebellion never hurt anyone, I always told them. Like being in a secret society. Inked but no one ever knowing.

This will lay the groundwork for the tension between the students and the older townsfolk. items.name: The Boss
items.contents:
I told him to lay off...
Boss never listened to anything but his gut.
Now we've got these two fools bickering over who should lead us.
Honestly, I'm more scared about what the Rust King's gonna do when he finds out the boss ain't around no more.
Maybe we just don't tell him.
Hold up in camp and figure it out.
As long as people keep passing by, we can survive on the pie.
But we need to tinker with this recipe as soon as possible. We can't have more people turning out like the boss.

items.name: The Coffee
items.contents:
It was never just a coffee shop. It was a meeting point. A chance to see neighbors, friends. Just knowing there were other people in this city that you recognized was a small piece of humanity you could buy with two creams and sugar.
-R

items.name: The Doctors
items.contents:
If you're looking for medical assistance, then it's strictly DIY at this point.
-R

items.name: The Drop
items.contents:
Careful now. Don't fall.
-R

items.name: The End
items.contents:
These are not mine. Not anymore. Perhaps they will give you the comfort that I have lost.
-R

items.name: The Evil Men
items.contents:
Even after the bombs fell, Charleston stood strong. My neighbors, my friends, held together. They rebuilt. A terrible thing had happened, yes, but I saw the good in the world, through them.
That has been washed away. Drowned. The madness of a few have destroyed the hopes of the many.
-R

items.name: The Great War
items.contents:
Munch's Memoirs: The Great War
People want to blame the Great War on Communism, but Communism's only fault was covering up the truth.
Back in the day, the Raiders had the power. We ruled these corporations and every major city. We had the military in our pocket and every corrupt politician in our corner. And I'm not talking nationwide. I'm talking worldwide. We were unstoppable... So of course, someone had to try, right?
These countries didn't nuke each other because of Communism. They nuked each other to stop the Raiders. But after all's said and done, look who's still standing.

items.name: The House
items.contents:
Sorry the way here is such a bother. This building has seen better days, but I'm glad you made it. Make yourself at home.
-R

items.name: The King's Witness VI
items.contents:
We encountered a Deathclaw.
He killed the brute swiftly, effortlessly.
He told me that he found kinship in the creatures.
They were hunters like him.
He had his men raise them from eggs for the arena.
I asked him if he saw the Deathclaws as his children.
He said this kingdom was his child. His seed, the blood spilled on its soil.
I did not prod further on this subject.
He said this story reminded him of something he wanted to show me.
We continued further down the road.
I pray and reflect on Genesis 9:2.

items.name: The Mound
items.contents:
I got stung good and it burns. God it burns hotter than I ever would have thought. They're all that mound, burrowed in deep. It can't get me up here but that damned bot, it's as bad as the venom. The last thing I hear is going to be corn trivia.
If you read this, stay off that mound.

items.name: The Nova Orbital Station
items.contents:
Munch's Memoirs: The Nova-Orbital-01
Long before we ever landed a man on the moon, USSA had already launched a top secret program to create the world's first space station: the Nova-Orbital-01. The space race was real, but the true mission was to gather information on the alien spies that infiltrated our planet.
The town of Flatwoods had already seen them. We knew they were out there, but we couldn't have a panic on our hands. We didn't know the alien motives, so the public could know nothing.
Once the Great War hit, the aliens made their move. They knocked old Nova-Orbital right out of the sky, and here she lies. We found her. We rebuilt her. And now she's Outpost-Crater-01, the best home in all of Appalachia.

items.name: The Old World
items.location: Burn CUT Athens Note Sport Car
items.contents:
Every day that goes by, I long more and more for those simple times I took for granted.
I miss good food and fresh water, sure, who doesn't. But to feel the wind rush through my hair as we cruised down the highway, I would give anything for one more ride.
Now we sit here, rotting away overlooking the now shattered roads. There never will be going back to those days. I'm just thankful I can still sneak up here past the military and watch the stars with you. To have you my old friend, is all I really need.

items.name: The Owner
items.contents:
I knew the man who lived here. It wasn't long before someone killed him for this house - sniped from one of the overlooking buildings. Don't let that happen to you.
-R

items.name: The Plan
items.contents:
The Plan
1. Finish costume show 2. Borrow any monster costume 3. Meet up by the Parson's barn at 1:00 am 4. We scare the hell out of Shelby at her damn shack

items.name: The Poultry Enthusiasts Guide to Shenandoah
items.contents:
21st I bumped into some travelers on the road and they were tucking into a giant fried turkey leg. It was so bizarre. I'd never imagined that those creatures could grow so large.
The travelers told me that the turkeys are feral and not to be trusted but they make for a great supper, if you can catch one.
I must find these creatures and study them: they'll make a great addition to my book. [pagebreak] 24th Today I saw a nye of pheasants gathered around a rather strange and large nest. I intended to take a closer look at these nests to see what they are made up of. [pagebreak] 25th
Brilliant day! Today I saw one of the aforementioned turkeys in one of the nests! These turkeys are marvelous creatures, but just as feral as the travelers described. [pagebreak] 27th God damn, I just saw one eat a Mole Rat!
They were just nesting as per usual, then one of them Moles popped out of the ground and in a flash, one snatched it with its claw!
It then began to shred the creature with it's razor sharp beak, throwing pieces into the air and swallowing them whole. This is far from what I'd expect from any bird none-the-less the turkey! [pagebreak] 28th I feel I must approach with caution, these creatures are dangerous, perhaps they are even plotting against me! Last night I could have sworn I heard them stalking around my camp.
Those turkeys are up to something...

items.name: The Power Plant
items.contents:
The hydroelectric plant powered a lot of Charleston. A little ironic for coal country, I always thought.
They were so close to getting it back up and running when it all happened.
-R

items.name: The Safe
items.contents:
It was open when I got here. I swear.
-R

items.name: The Shrink
items.contents:
Doctor Joseph was always busy treating anxiety and depression for office workers and politicians from the capitol.
It seems like a luxury, now, but sometimes nothing is more valuable than a talk with someone who will really listen.
-R

items.name: The Solution
items.contents:
I need to do something about my little "L.P." problem. I don't want to hurt the guy's feelings, but I can't stand him anymore.
Molly said I should get someone to take him out. I know she was joking, but I think it's a good idea. He'd probably be a wreck and get himself killed anyway, so I'm practically doing the guy a solid.
I think I'm going to ask Surge. She'll do it, especially if caps are involved. Plus, she can take him out without anyone even know. We don't call her "The Surgeon" for nothing. If she can take him out with one of those precision shots of hers, no one will ever know.

items.name: The View
items.contents:
Quite a view from here, don't you think?
-R

items.name: They got me good
items.contents:
Sorry fellas, they got me good. Stupid cavern used to be an easy spot to rest the night and score some long-forgotten goods, but... those big green guys came outta no where. Managed to outrun em, but... well you're probably looking at me, right?
Biggest joke of all is that I didn't score any loot. Just some whacko's poetry reading.
Sad that this is the last thing I'm gonna hear, but... Yeah, they got me good.

items.name: Things to Remember
items.contents: Things to Remember: - Always respond to Wren's communications. - Always listen to Wren's intel reports. - It's not funny to play dead. - Wren fights dirty when she's pissed off.

items.name: This Wasteland I Call Home
items.contents:
This Wasteland I Call Home by Reggie B.
You said my name, my heart was slain, In this wasteland we call home.
Under your spell, my world was hell, In this wasteland we call home.
You tore me down, Jerked me around, But how could I say no?
I played your game, You were insane, So how could I say no?
And with your knife, you took my life,
In this wasteland we call home.
You winked at me, and I was free, Of this wasteland I called home.

items.name: Thom and Molly
items.contents:
Thom and Molly,
LEAVE NOW!
Get out of Watoga! Do NOT try to stay at home.
Meet us at the Big Bend Tunnel!
Love,
Mom & Dad

items.name: To Mom
items.contents:
Mom, please come with us
I know I've asked so many times, but please don't stay here. Jeanie and I are going to leave with the next scavenger group later today. Curtis said he'll tell you about this place in detail, and he insists that it's better than dying here.
Staying here drinking that dirty water is going to kill you. This new place has plenty of clean food, water, and medicine. Just think about it, please. I'll keep contact as best I can, and I'll come back to travel with you if you decide to go.
I love you,
Max

items.name: To whoever else was an idiot
items.contents:
Joy Lynn told me that hunting down that old treasure wouldn't be a good idea, and I guess she'd be laughing if she knew. I'm sure she could probably figure it out from my disappearance, but for all she knows, I got strung up by some raiders. It'd be less embarrassing honestly.
Grandpa used to tell stories about this treasure from the 1950's or something, and lone behold it's real. He mentioned Coopers and Bulls from his research, but turns out it was the old blue Bullengrube Hole. It was easy enough to sink down with that rock, but no way I could hold my breath long enough to swim back up.
I ask you stranger, if you've got the gall to swim back out, and it's still around the 2090's, tell Joy Lynn you saw Leroy go down defending a family from some raiders.

items.name: Trouble with Radiation
items.contents:
So, the radiation issue is getting pretty bad. Ten of our guys just didn't wake up this morning. And, some other people are starting to lose their hair. I was brushing something off my cheek in the middle of the night. Thought it was just a fly, but I woke up and a large chunk of my cheek is missing. I think I peeled it off in my sleep. This shit is not going well.
I hate to admit it, but I am gonna send a message to the street rats and see if we can call for peace. They don't look like they're in good shape either and this little war game has gone on long enough.
Charles

items.name: Unsent Letter
items.contents: Dear Kirsch, See? I told you I'd write you. You really need to get over here and check out the Palace of the Winding Path. This place is your dream. Pack up the old chem box, and meet me at the Red Rocket Mega Stop. It'll be the start of your "spiritual journey." I met a guy there that's got stuff that'll make you fly. Just don't let any of the protectrons there catch you loitering. They're worse then cops. If worse comes to worse, see if you can find their control terminal. As long as you're at least somewhat coherent, I'm sure you can put those old tech skills to use and shut them down. - Jinny

It's been almost ten years since the Responders took you from me, and for once, I can take peace in the thought that you may be at rest. This is no longer the world we survived, nor the one we built. The Scorched have the upper hand now. They've got some mutated bat creatures that've been set loose, and they're destroying everything.
Harpers Ferry was wiped out. Everyone's fleeing for their lives. But I won't leave. I know you're here... somewhere.

items.name: Warning to Vincent
items.contents:
Hey Vincent,
I wanted to give you a heads up about a suspicious character that passed through here the other day. He was a sleazy, bald pig of a man named Keith Cooper. Initially he was charming, but when he saw I wasn't falling for his tricks, the mask came off. I know how gullible you can be Vin, and this asshole fancies himself quite the "opportunist".
Apparently he was in West Virginia the last few years but wasn't able to gain the ground he wanted with some group and had to fake his death. He must have heard about the way things work over here, and now believes he can climb his way to the top and build a new empire. I don't want you interacting with him and getting roped into some shit again. Honestly, I should have done the world a favor and just shot the guy.
Good news is, it sounds like West Virginia is resettling and there's pockets of good people. The Scorched Plague is still around, but less of an issue, so I'm heading out. Once I'm established, I'll come back for you and Lucy.
Stay out of trouble, -Dan

Doug, we're leaving
We kept telling those students that we shouldn't bring in all those people from the factory, and now we're all catching The Rot because of it. They already dug two burn pits, but it wasn't enough. Now they're not even bothering to cart them away, but burning them in the streets instead.
We'll do much better on our own away from all these morons. They can't even give us clean water here.

items.name: Welcome to Point Repose
items.contents:
If you're reading this you probably know that you're going feral. And you likely don't have much time, but how you face the twilight is your decision. Nobody is going to make you stay.
This place is a sanctuary for our kind. Hang on as long as you can, but when it's time to let go, travel through the Last Door. Nobody will hurt you in there.
Use the grounds, treat your fellow residents kindly, and take the time you need to make your peace.
- Maddox

items.name: What About Us?
items.contents:
Jerome,
I know your heart is in the right place, wanting to sneak out and take supplies to people in the countryside. But what about us? What about the fact that we need supplies too? What makes their lives more important than ours? Why shouldn't we go out and scavenge for ourselves? Don't bother answering. I know what you'll say.
I'll be gone by the time you look for me. Ellen

items.name: What's Real
items.contents:
Heidi would always say, "You gotta get off the drugs, Anna, they rot your brain," and I'd laugh. Man, it was funny at the time! But shit, now? She was right all along. I'm not even in the real world anymore.
I'm trapped in some bad trip nightmare. I tried sobering up, but it was worse. WAY WORSE. All the animals here look dead or halfway there. People look like they stepped right out of a horror movie to eat my brain, or what's fucking left of it.
I got a plan to get out of it. Drugs got me in here, they can get me out, so I'm gonna do them ALL. And when I wake up, it's stone cold sober for me, baby.

items.name: Where are you?
items.contents:
Abbie, Where are you? I've been waiting for hours. I can't wait any longer, but I wanted to tell you something.
I hope you find this note.
I hear you are thinking about going to Watoga. Don't. It's not safe. I don't know what, but it sounds like everyone there got killed or something. -R Fields

You're his handler. You fought for this project. Make sure it's worth our while.
I'm going to want a report in person this time, but I've relocated since we last spoke face-to-face. Meet me at Sal's Grinders in Beckley. The town's in bad shape right now, but the place is deserted. Nobody to listen in.
And remember to burn this note when you're done.
Wolf

cutContent.name: Squire Asher's Journal
cutContent.contents:
June 20, 2082
Finally found a good spot for Quercus to do his surveys. Squire Ramsay saw me hauling the desk up here and made a real sour face when she figured out what I had done with the old Handy we found off-duty. "Scrap metal", she called him. Me? I saw potential.
So I gave him a name and a purpose: document the creatures of the swamp. Ramsay said the higher-ups would reprimand me for wasting time learning about animals. The way I see it, every new monster that comes crawling out of the radiation is a potential threat, and threats need to be catalogued.
It's strange, but Quercus doesn't appear to see them that way. I did alter his behavior to gain the creatures' trust, but he talks to them more than he should; he's even started naming them.
If I could find him a new battery unit, maybe that would fix his behavior. I want him working around the clock to catalogue as much information as possible.
-Squire Asher

cutContent.name: Nathan Broadhurst's Autobiogrophy
cutContent.location: zzz NPE Note Nathan Red Sox
cutContent.contents:
My name is Nathan Broadhurst, and here is my story of how I went from a famous baseball player, to a lonely but content old man.
I can still remember, clear as day when it all started. It was the morning before the big game-The World Series. It was us versus Texas. I showed up early with Jim Walker and Matt Murtagh. Matt had been worried sick, because he was first up to pitch, so Jim and I were helping him warm up. Little did we realize the biggest day of our life was larger than we expected. I was up to bat when we felt everything shake. Thank God for Fenway's massive walls, otherwise we woulda been toast. We assumed it was an Earthquake at first, until that terrible sound, and the burst of dust overhead. I remember watching half the chairs in the outfield being blasted to Hell.
Once the worst of it appeared to be over, Matt was in a rush to head back to Atlanta to make sure his family was okay. Never found out if he made it back or not. I went with Jim and headed West so we could meet up with my fiance Janice, who was also Jim's sister. They had grown up in Charleston West Virginia. We were originally gonna take a more coastal route, but we heard that New York was even worse off than Boston. We ended up taking Highway 90 onto 84 until we joined a group in Hartford who was heading to Pittsburg. Shortly after we parted ways in Altoona, Jim and I ran into some trouble.
It was this little town called Bedford which had already walled themselves in. Some bald putz came storming out with his group of assholes on bikes. They pinned us down, tied us up, and locked us in an old bank. Luckily it didn't take us long to cut ourselves free, find our bats, and get onto the roof, but when we jumped onto the next building, someone shot Jim mi-air. He was dead before he hit the street below. He'd been my best friend for years, and I had just watched someone shoot him like he was nothing. I had no choice but to run before they got me too.
It nearly took me another week to make it to Charleston. When I got here, no one had seen or heard from Janice in weeks. I searched for months, but never did find her. For all I know, we passed her on the way here. After a few years, I decided to settle down with a group of welcoming and bright eyed settlers. We built our home here on the cliffs, and it is here I am content to die.
I leave behind my story and my once famous bat in the hopes that it'll inspire or help anyone who needs it.
